note: The County of Anjou — the ancestral domain of the Plantagenet/Angevin dynasty — was conquered by Philip II Augustus of France in 1204 simultaneously with Normandy. John of England's military failures (inability to relieve Château Gaillard, failure at Bouvines in 1214 against a Poitevin rebellion backed by Philip) confirmed French control. Anjou's absorption with its associated counties (Maine, Touraine) gave France the Loire Valley heartland. A restored Angevin dynasty (the House of Valois-Anjou) received Anjou as an appanage in 1360, but it reverted to the crown on René I's death (1480).

_quarry.structural_significance: The loss of Anjou, along with Normandy, eliminates the Angevin Empire as a political reality; the Loire Valley's absorption transforms France into the most powerful kingdom in Western Europe; the Anjou claim to Naples (inherited through the appanage line) feeds the Italian Wars
